decisions.rationale: 'Tay-Sachs disease' names one specific disease (the title mention) and is not a family of diseases or a modifier, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease mentions); Examples 1 and 5

decisions.rationale: 'infantile Tay-Sachs disease' refers to one specific form of the disease. The minimum necessary span that expresses the most specific form includes 'infantile', so the whole string is annotated as one Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span of text); Example 2 and Example 1 (prefer the whole string)

decisions.rationale: 'TSD' is the abbreviation for Tay-Sachs disease, used here as a synonymous mention referring to the same specific disease. Abbreviations are annotated as a separate mention from the long form, and it is used as a noun referring to the disease, not as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6 (synonymous mentions, abbreviation definitions); Example 5

decisions.rationale: In 'an Italian TSD proband', 'TSD' is a disease mention that modifies the noun 'proband' (a person), so it functions as a Modifier of another concept rather than as a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers for other concepts); Example for colorectal cancer modifier
